skill.name: azure-compute
skill.description: Guides Azure VM and VM Scale Set planning, pricing, provisioning, capacity reservations, machine management enrollment, and RDP or SSH troubleshooting.
skill.summary: Plan, create, price, and troubleshoot Azure compute resources with guided Azure workflows.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from markdown links, Azure documentation URLs, public SSH key examples, and IaC templates. Confirmed risks are operational: selected troubleshooting commands can change VM credentials, firewall access, networking, or SELinux state, and the GitHub PR delivery path lacks documented validation for shell placeholders. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: GitHub PR commands interpolate user-controlled repo, branch, path, and VM values.
remediation.suggestion: Validate allowed characters, quote every shell argument, and prefer structured tool calls over generated shell strings.

remediation.issue: VM recovery commands can reset credentials or change remote access controls.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval for each state-changing command, show the affected resource, and provide rollback steps.

remediation.issue: Firewall and SELinux recovery guidance can weaken guest security.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer read-only diagnostics first, use temporary targeted rules, and document how to restore the previous policy.

remediation.issue: Terraform quickstart uses a third-party public IP lookup service.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before making the lookup or provide an Azure-owned or manual alternative for the source CIDR value.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled Shell Placeholders In PR Workflow
semantic_findings.description: The GitHub PR delivery workflow accepts repo, branch, and target path values from the user, then places those values in shell commands without documented validation or escaping. A malicious branch or path could turn infrastructure delivery into command injection if an agent executes the commands.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The file gathers user-controlled repo, branch, and path strings and later interpolates them directly into gh, git, mkdir, and git add commands. The workflow is legitimate, but missing validation makes injection plausible.

semantic_findings.title: Privileged VM Recovery Commands Require Strong Approval
semantic_findings.description: The troubleshooting references include commands to reset passwords, reset SSH configuration, enable RDP, open SSH firewall rules, unlock accounts, and set SELinux permissive. These are legitimate recovery actions, but they can change access controls and host security state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited commands directly alter credentials, SSH/RDP access, firewall policy, account state, or SELinux enforcement. The files include warnings, so the issue is operational risk rather than malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Azure compute work requires many choices across VM size, cost, networking, and access recovery. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured Azure VM and VMSS workflows.
actual_capabilities: Routes Azure compute requests to VM creation, recommendation, troubleshooting, capacity reservation, or management workflows.
Compares VM and VMSS options using SKU, image, quota, region, and pricing guidance.
Builds Azure VM deployment plans for az CLI, Bicep, Terraform, or Azure MCP apply flows.
Guides RDP, SSH, NSG, firewall, credential, and VM agent troubleshooting with pre-flight checks.
Explains capacity reservation groups and VM association or disassociation steps.
Guides Essential Machine Management enrollment prerequisites and validation steps.
limitations: It does not authenticate to Azure by itself or grant missing subscription permissions.
Live resource creation needs a connected Azure MCP server or a user-run CLI workflow.
Pricing and SKU availability can change and should be verified during the session.
Recovery commands can change VM access and should be approved before execution.

use_cases.title: Choose a VM size for a workload
use_cases.description: Compare candidate VM families, estimate cost, and check quota before a deployment decision.

use_cases.title: Generate repeatable VM infrastructure
use_cases.description: Create a reviewed plan and render it as az CLI, Bicep, Terraform, or Azure MCP inputs.

use_cases.title: Recover VM connectivity
use_cases.description: Diagnose RDP, SSH, firewall, network, credential, and VM agent problems with safety checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a basic Linux VM
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a small Ubuntu VM in eastus for development. Recommend safe defaults and show the decisions I must approve.

prompt_templates.title: Compare VM options
prompt_templates.scenario: User needs price and fit guidance.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Azure VM options for a low-cost web backend with 2 to 4 vCPUs. Include pricing, quota checks, and tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Generate infrastructure output
prompt_templates.scenario: User has approved a plan and wants IaC.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the approved plan to generate Terraform for the VM. Include variables, outputs, validation notes, and cleanup guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot blocked access
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced recovery for a production VM.
prompt_templates.prompt: I cannot SSH to my Azure Linux VM. Walk through safe diagnostics first, then propose recovery commands that require approval.

output_examples.input: I need a cheap Linux VM for a temporary test service.
output_examples.output: A decision table with region, VM size, image, disk, network, public IP, SSH source range, estimated cost, and approval status.

output_examples.input: Create Terraform for the approved VM plan.
output_examples.output: A Terraform delivery summary with files to create, variables to review, deployment steps, verification steps, and cleanup notes.

output_examples.input: RDP to my Windows VM times out.
output_examples.output: A diagnostic path covering OS confirmation, NSG checks, public IP checks, guest firewall status, and approved recovery options.

best_practices: Run read-only validation before creating, changing, or repairing Azure compute resources.
Restrict SSH or RDP ingress to a trusted source range instead of the open internet.
Review the plan card and cost estimate before generating or applying infrastructure.
anti_patterns: Do not skip approval before live Azure MCP apply or VM recovery commands.
Do not paste private SSH keys, passwords, or long-lived service principal secrets into chat.
Do not open SSH or RDP to all sources unless the user explicitly accepts the risk.

faq.question: Can this skill create Azure resources?
faq.answer: It can guide creation and prepare artifacts. Live creation requires Azure MCP access or user-run Azure CLI commands.

faq.question: Does it support both VMs and VM Scale Sets?
faq.answer: Yes. It routes single VM and VMSS requests and asks for scale-set details when needed.

faq.question: Can it estimate VM pricing?
faq.answer: Yes. It uses Azure retail pricing guidance and recommends verification because prices can change.

faq.question: Can it troubleshoot SSH and RDP issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers NSG, public IP, guest firewall, credentials, VM agent, and service configuration checks.

faq.question: Does it need my Azure credentials?
faq.answer: The skill does not collect credentials. Azure actions depend on your existing MCP or CLI authentication.

faq.question: Is it safe to use for production workloads?
faq.answer: Use it with change review, least-privilege access, cost checks, and explicit approval for any live operation.
